Self-Hosted AI Gateway for Enterprise AI Governance

One control point for every AI call your company makes. Provider keys stay on your servers, access follows policy, spend is budgeted and charged back, and every request leaves an audit trail without storing prompts or responses.

Current release: v2.14.0 (availability: signed release assets and successful release workflow)

SiftGate is an MIT-licensed AI gateway that you run on your own infrastructure. Business apps, coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, SDKs and MCP tools send requests to SiftGate instead of calling AI providers directly. SiftGate decides who may call which model, which provider key is used, what the request may cost, and what evidence is kept, before the request leaves your network.

Why Enterprises Put A Gateway In Front Of AI

AI adoption usually starts with a few provider keys. At company scale it turns into a governance problem:

What breaks as AI use grows What SiftGate changes
Shadow AI and key sprawl. Engineers paste provider keys into editors, agents and MCP tools. Nobody can say who uses which model, and offboarding cannot revoke access. Provider keys stay inside the gateway. Teams and people get scoped, revocable Gateway API keys limited to approved endpoints, modalities, nodes and models.
Security review blocks rollout. Security and legal teams worry that a new proxy becomes a store of prompts, source code and customer data. Metadata-only by default: no prompts, responses, raw headers, source code, diffs, tool payloads, media bytes or resolved secrets are stored unless an operator explicitly enables it.
Spend arrives as one unexplained bill. Costs cannot be attributed to teams or projects, and rotating keys breaks provider prompt caches. Budgets at global, namespace, team and key scope, workspace price books, chargeback exports, and cache-aware credential pools that keep cache locality across keys.
One provider outage stops everyone. Rate limits and incidents halt work, and nobody can explain why traffic moved. Fallback chains, circuit breakers and per-key credential failover, with a route explanation for every request.

Four Governance Pillars

1. Access and policy. One ingress for OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible chat, embeddings, rerank, media, Batch and MCP tool traffic, routed to any configured provider, including Gemini, Bedrock and Azure. Permissions are the intersection of Gateway API key, Team and Policy Namespace rules, and an empty intersection fails closed. Per-key model pools route an exact chat model across approved nodes. The Dashboard has authentication on by default, fixed admin/operator/viewer roles, Workspaces, invitations and optional OIDC. Quick connect creates a scoped key and a bound coding agent profile in one step. Every request refused by a key permission, a key's rate limit or a budget is recorded as metadata under Blocked requests, by key, reason and minute.

2. Data protection and audit. Call logs, route traces, sessions, MCP calls, batch jobs and guardrail findings record metadata, not content. The optional local guardrails plugin redacts or blocks PII, secrets, prompt injection and policy matches, and records findings as metadata. Management actions go to a hash-chained audit log, and configuration changes are versioned with validation-first rollback. Full Gateway API keys are shown once; provider secrets never appear in Dashboard APIs, logs or exports. A read-only privacy posture lists every setting that would keep prompt or response content and whether the running configuration has turned it on.

3. Cost control. Daily token and cost budgets at global, namespace, team and key scope reject over-budget requests with budget_exceeded. Workspace price books, admission previews, a cost report, chargeback CSV/JSON exports, anomaly evidence and cache-savings reporting show where money goes. Cache-aware credential pools reduce duplicated prompt-cache warmup across parallel keys.

4. Reliability and operations. Smart routing with compatibility filters, fallback chains, circuit breakers and credential cooldowns. Route Explanation shows which candidates were selected, skipped or rejected and why. Start on SQLite, then move to PostgreSQL, optional Redis, Docker, Kubernetes or Helm, OIDC, log sinks and OpenTelemetry. Customer release kits are signed with Sigstore provenance, and the optional host Operator applies upgrades only from reviewed, approved plans.

Read the enterprise overview for the full governance model, or hand the security and compliance brief to your security reviewers.

The Dashboard follows the same structure. Its sidebar groups work into Access & Policy, Agents & Tools, Models & Routing, Cost Control and Audit & Operations, with previews and evaluation tools in a collapsed Labs group. Related pages appear as tabs inside each section, and every existing URL still works. The Governance Overview opens with the posture a reviewer asks about first: whether any setting keeps content, how many requests policy refused in the last 24 hours, spend against the daily limit, and runtime health. See the Dashboard guide.

See It In A 30-Minute Evaluation

Each scenario below is part of the PoC playbook, which scripts the full demo with pass criteria.

Govern a coding agent with a scoped key. In Coding Agents → Quick connect, pick the tool, then gateway routing or one model, and optionally a policy scope, daily cost and per-minute limit. SiftGate creates the scoped Gateway API key and a bound Agent Profile together and renders the setup snippet. The engineer's machine never holds a provider key, and coding-auto maps to policy-respecting smart routing.

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:2099
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<SIFTGATE_GATEWAY_API_KEY>
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=coding-auto

Pool provider keys without losing prompt cache. Several upstream keys live inside one logical node. cache_aware keeps a session on the key that already holds its provider prompt cache and moves to another key on 429, 5xx or timeouts.

nodes:
  - id: enterprise-anthropic
    name: "Enterprise Anthropic"
    protocol: messages
    base_url: "https://api.anthropic.com"
    endpoint: "/v1/messages"
    auth_type: x-api-key
    credentials:
      - id: primary
        api_key: "${env:ANTHROPIC_POOL_KEY_PRIMARY}"
      - id: backup
        api_key: "${env:ANTHROPIC_POOL_KEY_BACKUP}"
    credential_pool:
      enabled: true
      strategy: cache_aware
      sticky_by: agent_session
      cooldown_ms: 60000
      retry_on_status: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

Credential ids appear in logs; secret values never do.

Explain any request without storing it. Every response carries an x-siftgate-request-id header. Open /route-decisions/<request-id> in the Dashboard to see the selected and rejected candidates, policy filters, credential hit, cache effect, fallback reason, latency and cost estimate. The prompt and response were never written to disk.

Show what the gateway refused, and why. Point a key with a narrow scope at a model, endpoint or budget it does not cover. Each refusal is recorded as metadata in Request Logs → Blocked requests, grouped per key, reason and minute, with filters for both. Refusals stay out of call logs, so success rates, routing samples and cost reports are unchanged.

By default SiftGate stores operational metadata: request id, selected node and model, credential id and retry count, latency, status, token usage, cost estimate, policy labels, fallback reason, cache evidence and route explanation. It does not store prompts, responses, raw provider headers, provider keys, tool payloads, media bytes, hidden reasoning text or resolved secrets unless a feature is explicitly configured to retain content.

The open-source gateway is complete on its own. AI requests never need to pass through a hosted service, and no control plane is required.

Quick Start

For a versioned, persistent Docker installation, use the customer install kit (中文). Source availability does not mean the newest image is already published.

To run from source:

git clone https://github.com/seanbabalala/SiftGate.git
cd SiftGate
# Select Node >=22.13.0 <23 using .nvmrc (nvm install && nvm use when available).
npm run runtime:check
npm install
cd frontend && npm install && cd ..
cp gateway.config.example.yaml gateway.config.yaml
cp .env.example .env
npm run build
# Configure dashboard.password (or OIDC) in the private YAML before this step.
npm start

SiftGate loads .env automatically. Example provider nodes use secret references such as ${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}, so the Dashboard starts before provider keys are filled in. A source installation needs dashboard.password or OIDC configured first: a plaintext password is hashed on startup, and missing credentials fail closed with no generated password in logs. The customer kit uses a one-time activation code instead; follow the documentation shipped with your kit version.

Surface URL
Dashboard http://localhost:2099/dashboard
OpenAPI http://localhost:2099/docs
Gateway http://localhost:2099

Add one upstream node, create a Gateway API key in the Dashboard, then send a request:

curl http://localhost:2099/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer ${SIFTGATE_API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "auto",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain SiftGate in one sentence."}]
  }'

For a container-first path, use Docker Quickstart.

Catalog data is operational guidance, not a billing authority. Local node pricing, models_pricing and catalog.override.yaml remain the operator-controlled source of truth. Live provider evidence is tracked in the Provider Smoke Matrix.

## Where SiftGate Fits

SiftGate is built for governing AI traffic your company owns: provider keys, agent access, MCP tools, policy, budgets, route evidence and metadata-only audit in one self-hosted system.

If your main job is Consider
Governing company-owned AI traffic across apps, agents and tools SiftGate
Public API resale, prepaid wallets or reseller billing One API or New API
The lightest cost-first model router for one agent or app Manifest
A developer-centric multi-provider proxy LiteLLM Proxy

SiftGate is not an API resale platform, billing wallet, hosted prompt store, workflow engine, model marketplace or mandatory SaaS control plane, and it does not turn third-party catalog prices into billing truth. It builds on ideas from Manifest, One API, New API and LiteLLM, and we are grateful for their public work. The full capability matrix, acknowledgements and committed benchmark evidence are in Comparison and Performance.

Enterprise Support

SiftGate runs without any hosted service. If your team needs help with deployment, provider onboarding, a security review or a guided PoC, contact the maintainer on Telegram: @seanbbuu. Provider credentials, policy, billing and compliance stay under your operational control.

Contributing

The public repository tracks source, examples, docs, tests and deployment manifests only. Local runtime config, databases, catalog sync cache and private notes are ignored. Before opening a PR, run:

npm run public:check
npm run docs:check
npm run build
cd frontend && npm test && npm run build

Release branches also run the broader matrix in the Release Checklist. Maintainers publishing images follow the formal image release runbook (中文) and its state gate.
